purpose: Turn Elementor JSON source evidence into reproducible pinned-baseline WordPress/Elementor controlled-runtime evidence with source validation, official Template Library import, semantic importer roundtrip, registered widget inventory and cross-browser responsive rendering. Optional Elementor Pro is run-resolved unless an explicit version constraint is introduced and is therefore evidenced only for the exact installed version captured in that run's runtime inventory.

caller.surface_rule: Chat web/desktop may use the exposed GitHub connector and remote GitHub Actions runtime. This does not imply local repository, terminal, WP-CLI or target-site access. Local or target claims still require their own surface/preflight.
caller.qa_handoff: website-qa-checklist for staging/live/browser acceptance beyond this disposable controlled runtime

required_when: new or screenshot-reconstructed Elementor JSON needs a runtime or visual claim
existing Elementor JSON changes structure, widgets, widget settings, responsive behavior or dependencies
the user asks to test, scan, render, preview, screenshot, verify widgets, verify Pro or check import behavior
source-valid JSON is about to be described as runtime-valid, importer-valid or visually correct
optional_when: the task is a source-only audit or planning task and no runtime, importer or visual claim is needed
forbidden_when: input contains secrets, credentials, personal data or client-confidential content while this repository is public
the task requires exact target-site IDs or target compatibility without target inventory or staging evidence
the task is a production or live-site mutation

why: detect malformed Classic or Atomic Elementor structures before import
detect missing or unavailable Elementor widgets before target import
check JSON against widgets and controls registered by a real Elementor runtime
exercise Elementor's documented Template Library importer instead of treating direct postmeta writes as import proof
detect semantic importer drift while ignoring only volatile Elementor element IDs
prove that WordPress and Elementor can render the importer-produced template data in a disposable environment
produce Chromium, Firefox and WebKit evidence at desktop, tablet and mobile viewports
separate source-only, controlled-runtime and target evidence

before_run: read runtime-contract.json from main and verify repository, branch, workflow and evidence role
classify editor family, dependency mode, target objects and risk with the Elementor skill
sanitize public-repository inputs and keep secrets outside committed files
write or update the canonical test JSON under templates/
optionally provide target/inventory.json only when it is sanitized and safe for this public repository
run: let the Elementor JSON QA workflow start from the main change or workflow_dispatch
resolve the resulting workflow run and require both Static JSON audit and Elementor runtime preview to complete successfully
readback: check dependency audit, runtime inventory, source/runtime/deep audits, importer roundtrip reports, render manifests and Elementor Pro status
inspect Chromium, Firefox and WebKit desktop/tablet/mobile screenshot metadata before making a browser claim
record open target, editor reopen/save/re-export, accessibility and staging tests separately
iterate: on a confirmed source, dependency, importer, roundtrip or render defect, repair the canonical source and rerun
on a visual mismatch, edit the canonical JSON and compare the next screenshots
never convert controlled-runtime success into target_verified or production_observed without later evidence

inputs.target_inventory: target/inventory.json (optional and only when sanitized for a public repository; confidential inventories require a private controlled runtime)
inputs.elementor_pro_secret: ELEMENTOR_PRO_LICENSE_KEY (optional GitHub Actions secret; never commit the value)
inputs.reference_visual: kept outside this public repository when confidential; used by the calling assistant for comparison

baseline.dependency_policy: direct npm versions are exact; npm audit blocks high/critical findings; a committed npm lockfile remains required for a fully immutable npm dependency graph; optional Elementor Pro is resolved from Elementor's official Composer repository per run unless an explicit version constraint is added, and the exact installed Pro version must be taken from runtime-inventory.json for any Pro-specific claim

pipeline: run source-level classic/widget auditor and deep Classic/Atomic structural validator
run validator and semantic-roundtrip unit tests
audit npm dependencies and fail on high/critical findings
start pinned disposable WordPress/PHP with wp-env
install pinned Elementor Core and Hello Elementor
optionally install and activate Elementor Pro from Elementor's official Composer repository and use the exact installed version captured in runtime-inventory.json as run-specific provenance
export the registered Elementor widget and control inventory and verify pinned runtime versions
audit every source template against the runtime and optional sanitized target inventory
import every source template through wp elementor library import
export the newest imported library item's semantic document data and compare it against source while ignoring only volatile element IDs
render importer-produced JSON into isolated Elementor Canvas pages
run Chromium, Firefox and WebKit browser checks at desktop, tablet and mobile viewports with reduced-motion, console, request, image and overflow checks
upload audit reports, importer outputs, runtime inventory, render manifests, Pro status and screenshots as workflow artifacts
deactivate the temporary Pro license when used and destroy the runtime

can_support: Classic and documented Atomic source-structure validation within implemented validator scope
runtime widget availability in the disposable environment
successful Elementor Template Library importer acceptance
semantic preservation of content and page_settings across importer storage while ignoring only volatile element IDs
successful disposable WordPress/Elementor render of importer-produced JSON
Chromium, Firefox and WebKit checks at the configured desktop, tablet and mobile viewports
does_not_prove: editor reopen/save or a target/UI re-export roundtrip
site-specific object IDs, target globals, Classes/Variables, conditions or dynamic data
Elementor Pro behavior when the Pro secret was not present for the run
cross-run Elementor Pro version reproducibility when Pro was resolved without an explicit version constraint
pixel-perfect visual equivalence without an approved reference baseline

iteration.on_failure: Repair only confirmed JSON, dependency, importer, roundtrip or render defects; never invent unknown Atomic, Pro, add-on or site-object data; then rerun the same pipeline.
iteration.on_visual_mismatch: Adjust the canonical JSON, rerun and compare new browser artifacts against the approved reference outside the public repository.
iteration.formal_final_gate: After the last implementation change, require two stable green final rounds for the covered controlled-runtime scope before handoff to staging/QA.

privacy.rule: Do not commit confidential client JSON, private screenshots, credentials, license keys, personal data, secret URLs or confidential target inventories. Use a private runtime/repository or sanitized fixtures instead.
privacy.secret_handling: ELEMENTOR_PRO_LICENSE_KEY must exist only as a GitHub Actions secret and must never be logged or committed.
